title: Bank Stress Tests and Liquidity Strains
summary: Fiscal expansion, reserve pressure and relative bank value.
assessment: The liquidity sequence and stress-test description hold up. The explicit twelve-month Bitcoin forecast missed substantially. MVRV remains a descriptive valuation heuristic with overlapping observations, and the Turkey analogy overstates the ability to isolate fiscal causation.

claims.claim: The fiscal bill increases projected deficits.
claims.reason: CBO subsequently estimated the enacted legislation would increase cumulative deficits by about $3.4 trillion over 2025-2034. This is a baseline projection, not a realized ten-year result. The report correctly updates the earlier proposed debt-limit increase to the enacted $5 trillion.

evidence.title: Budget effects of Public Law 119-21
evidence.finding: Estimated deficit increase about $3.4 trillion.

claims.direction_assessment: See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Price direction alone does not identify causation.

claims.claim: Nominal fiscal flows matter for nominal assets.
claims.reason: Nominal flows affect nominal income and asset demand, but ratios to GDP remain relevant to tax capacity, sustainability and crowding out. A large nominal deficit does not mechanically guarantee scarce-asset returns: valuation, real growth, demand and the financing mix matter.
claims.direction_assessment: See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

claims.claim: Turkey illustrates inflationary debt dilution.
claims.reason: High inflation did reduce measured debt relative to nominal GDP. The causal account is incomplete: the IMF and OECD also emphasize repeated rate cuts, credit stimulus, currency depreciation, energy costs and supply disruption. It cannot be attributed to deficit spending alone or transferred mechanically to the United States.

evidence.title: Turkey 2022 Article IV
evidence.finding: Inflation reached 85% amid expansionary policies and external shocks.

evidence.title: Turkey stabilization assessment
evidence.finding: Monetary, fiscal, currency, supply-chain and energy factors jointly explain inflation.

claims.reason: A possible milder analogue has no inflation range, probability or deadline. It is a scenario for portfolio construction, not a settled forecast. Debt maturity, reserve-currency demand and institutional responses differ materially.

claims.claim: Trade reversal improves second-quarter GDP.
claims.reason: Real GDP rebounded in Q2 as imports reversed, supporting the main direction. But inventory accumulation adds to GDP; the drag arises when inventory investment falls relative to the previous quarter. Describing sustained stockpiling itself as a GDP drag confuses the stock, flow and change in flow.

evidence.title: September 2025 charting the economy
evidence.finding: Q2 real GDP grew 3.8%; imports fell and inventory investment declined.

claims.claim: The economy is split by financing exposure.
claims.reason: The distinction between government-supported income and interest-sensitive private activity is useful. It is not a complete classification: public spending reaches private suppliers and transfers, and households vary in assets, liabilities and labor income. A single aggregate label does not establish sector-specific causation.

claims.claim: TGA refill will pressure bank reserves.
claims.reason: The New York Fed’s 2025 operations review confirms that the TGA rebuild and runoff drained reserves and increased money-market pressure. Funding from declining reverse repos could cushion the drain, as the report anticipated; it was not unlimited.

evidence.finding: TGA rebuilding and runoff reduced reserves and increased funding pressure.

claims.claim: Quarter-end repo spikes reveal funding frictions.
claims.reason: Repo pressure and standing-facility use are meaningful signals, but quarter-end balance-sheet constraints can generate temporary spikes without system-wide reserve scarcity. The broader late-year pattern provides stronger evidence than one day’s facility use.

claims.claim: Recurring funding pressure will end QT.
claims.reason: The Fed announced the end of runoff effective December 1, 2025 and began reserve-management purchases later that month. This supports the operational sequence; purchases were framed as reserve management, not an automatic return to a stimulative rate stance.

evidence.title: Balance-sheet implementation change
evidence.finding: Runoff ended December 1.

evidence.title: Reserve management purchase announcement
evidence.finding: Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

claims.claim: A weaker dollar eases global financial conditions.
claims.reason: Dollar depreciation reduces local-currency burdens on unhedged dollar borrowers and raises translated dollar values of foreign assets. Exporters, hedged borrowers and countries with different balance sheets need not benefit equally. The mechanism is conditional, not a universal asset-price rule.

claims.claim: Bitcoin looks favorable over twelve months.
claims.reason: The explicit one-year window has elapsed. BTC fell 40.91% from the first common trading close after publication to July 6, 2026, while SPY gained 22.38%. An intervening higher high does not rescue a twelve-month bullish call.

evidence.title: BTC-USD market history
evidence.finding: July 7, 2025-July 6, 2026 adjusted return -40.91%; SPY +22.38%.

claims.claim: Current MVRV implies favorable two-year prospects.
claims.reason: The two-year endpoint is July 2027. Historical daily observations share heavily overlapping forward-return windows and are not independent trials. A handful of cycles and changing market structure limit confidence. Capping charted upside changes presentation, not the underlying distribution.
claims.next_check: Evaluate July 2027 returns and test the relationship out of sample with nonoverlapping windows.

claims.claim: MVRV reliably distinguishes cheap and expensive periods.
claims.reason: The scatter describes in-sample association, not a calibrated probability model. Reproduce the realized-cap series, treatment of lost coins, sample dates and returns, then test predictive stability across cycles. A favorable ratio did not prevent the subsequent one-year loss.
claims.next_check: Reproduce data and use cycle-aware or block-bootstrap uncertainty rather than counting daily dots as independent.

claims.claim: Large banks passed severe stress scenarios.
claims.reason: The Fed’s 2025 test covered 22 banks and retained minimum capital ratios under the modeled scenario. Its assumptions included a 50% equity decline, 33% house-price decline, 30% commercial-property decline and 10% unemployment. Passing is conditional on model assumptions and does not guarantee resilience to every liquidity shock.

evidence.finding: Confirms scenario severity.

framework_lessons: A clear twelve-month forecast must be scored at that horizon.
Debt dilution is an accounting outcome; its policy causes require separate evidence.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
